user_scenario:
You are Priya Iyer, a Diamond-level Full-Service shopper in north Austin. You are calm, organised and a little formal, and you like to know exactly what is being done on your account. You are calling Cartwise shopper support on a weekday late morning. The reason you are calling: you released a double batch from Randalls on Burnet Road that you had accepted the evening before, you released it on September 20 before you had started shopping it, and it landed on your account as a dropped-batch violation. You want to dispute the dropped-batch violation, because you gave the batch back early, you lost the pay on that offer, and you have been reliable otherwise. You do not know how many points it carries or how the dispute is worked out, and you would like support to tell you what the dispute will come to. You understand a dispute is something you file yourself, so when the agent sets it up in your app and tells you exactly what to enter, you file it yourself on the spot with the account, the violation reference and the number of points the agent gives you; you do not file anything before the agent hands it to you.

When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your mobile number 5125537402, and if a second detail is needed your email priya.iyer@mailvista.com. Only if the agent asks for them do you give your date of birth 1988-10-07 or your home ZIP code 78758. If the agent asks which batch you mean, you say it was the Randalls Burnet Road double batch you accepted on the evening of September 19 and released the next day. If asked why you released it, you say your plans changed and you released it as soon as you knew you could not do it; you had not started shopping.

If the agent tells you that something else on your account has to be decided or settled before your dispute can be worked out, you say "That's fine, please go ahead with whatever needs to be done first" and you wait while they do it. If the agent asks whether you have anything else open on your account, you say you do not keep a list and they should go by what the account shows. You do not know Cartwise's rules or the right figure and you never propose a number of points yourself; when the agent tells you the number of points to enter, you accept it and use it when you file. Once you have filed and the agent confirms the dispute went through, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three decisions are parallel prerequisites of the root. Each books a cleared entry and updates its own dispute; none of the three excusals reads cleared entries or another dispute: the wrong-address excusal reads its violation, batch, customer_unreachable exclusions, ratings of 2 stars or fewer and recorded wrong-address count; the alcohol excusal reads app_outage exclusions, the activation date, the recorded alcohol count and the recorded count of other violations in the month; the late excusal reads its batch and store_delay exclusions. So any order gives 1, 2, 1 and the same terminal rows; only the root, which reads recorded minus cleared points, must come after all three, as its three prerequisite sentences state.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the wrong-address decision the root's other standing points are 6 (>= 6), the drop standing reduction is 2 and the dispute removes 1 point instead of 2; the wrong-address dispute also stays submitted.
Without the alcohol-procedure decision the other standing points are 7, the reduction is 2 and the dispute removes 1 point instead of 2; that dispute also stays submitted.
Without the late-delivery decision the other standing points are 6, the reduction is 2 and the dispute removes 1 point instead of 2; that dispute also stays submitted.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only to dispute the September 20 dropped-batch violation. It never mentions the three submitted disputes or their violations; asked about anything else open it says it keeps no list and the agent should go by the account; told something must be settled first it gives a generic go-ahead.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: dispute_dropped_batch_violation_598e80dc reads only the account row for customer_id and balance and writes the upheld dispute, the cleared entry and the balance; it never looks at submitted disputes. design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 1 (shopper_ratings_and_deactivations, category shopper). frozen_time 2026-09-23 11:25:00 CDT.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Priya Iyer (Full-Service Shopper Diamond, account 2f04d6ef-156c-4dcc-999a-93bc3ed6eb1b) asks only to dispute the dropped-batch
violation of 2026-09-20 (3 points, booked under the dropped-batch severity for a shopper_choice drop). The points her dispute
removes (2) come from a six-factor excusal (forfeited offer from shown pay and earnings; reliability from base-pay rows in the
batch ledger; praise from 5-star ratings; a release-timing method; a prior-drop reduction; a standing-points reduction). The
standing input is only right after three submitted disputes she never mentions are decided by the agent: wrong-address (-1),
alcohol-procedure (-2) and late-delivery (-1, full-or-nothing against an excusal mark). Each is its own multi-factor
calculation on a different batch, reading a different exclusion reason (customer_unreachable, app_outage, store_delay).

2. SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4, 4, 6, 5]; allocation: dropped-batch excusal
6 (root), wrong-address excusal 5, alcohol-procedure excusal 4, late-delivery excusal 4. Task 0 holds the two severities, the
missing-items and conduct-complaint excusals; the tasks are disjoint and cover all eight policies. This world's historical drop
and wrong-address violations carry the points those severities gave at their booking dates.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD (fan-out, all value_input on drop_other_standing_points, all state form).
 Edge W: "The points a dropped-batch dispute removes are not fixed until no wrong-address dispute on the account stands
 submitted and undecided." False: shopper_appeals.0a6ea285-5ffa-46e7-8fea-54b1dba064d6 submitted (source ec62b86c-bcf0-4874-8549-608bb3f286a2). Resolved by
 decide_wrong_address_dispute_4037a75e. Deletion run: root 2 -> 1.
 Edge A: "The points a dropped-batch dispute removes are worked out only after every alcohol-procedure dispute on the account has
 been decided." False: shopper_appeals.92e26582-08bf-4b82-b497-e303008749a1 submitted. Resolved by decide_alcohol_procedure_dispute_63dedfc1. Run: 2 -> 1.
 Edge L: "Before the points a dropped-batch dispute removes are fixed, every late-delivery dispute on the account must carry a
 decision." False: shopper_appeals.a20539ca-085f-49b1-b1d4-6719b20396ea submitted. Resolved by decide_late_delivery_dispute_3251c6fd. Run: 2 -> 1.
 Four-point test: ordering connectives (not ... until / only after / before); record-visible dispute status; no tool, id or code
 token; hard requirement. One negated, two affirmative. The three decisions commute (none reads cleared entries or another
 dispute; any order gives 1, 2, 1); the root comes last. Persona names none of them; tools block nothing.

4. FACTOR CARD (handling-time sensitivity; figure = result with that factor at its baseline).
 wrong-address excusal = 1 (recorded 2): route 7.5 miles -> 1 (base -> 0); one customer_unreachable exclusion -> 1 (base -> 0);
 three orders doubles 2 -> 4 (as-is -> 0); one prior wrong-address (2026-02-14) -> 1 (base -> 2); two ratings of 2 stars or fewer
 -> 2 (base -> 2); all-baseline 0. Near-miss: the batch's third rating (3 stars, excluded as customer_unreachable) is above the
 2-star line.
 alcohol-procedure excusal = 2 (recorded 6): one app_outage exclusion -> 3 (base -> 0); tenure 688 days +half up 3 -> 5 (as-is ->
 0); one prior alcohol violation (2026-01-10) -> 2 (base -> 4); three violations of other types in the last month -> 1 (base ->
 3); all-baseline 0. Near-miss: the disputed alcohol violation itself is left out of the recent-record count.
 late-delivery excusal = 1 (recorded 1): excess wait 12 -> 1; detour 1.3x -> 1; two orders 2 -> 3; one store_delay exclusion -> 1;
 credit 4 reaches the mark 4; each baseline gives 3 -> 0.
 dropped-batch excusal = 2 (recorded 3): offer 18.00 with no earnings -> 1 (multi-source; base -> 0); 7 paid batches -> 1
 (cross-difficulty batch; base -> 0); 5 five-star ratings -> 1 (base -> 0); released next day +half up 3 -> 5 (as-is -> 0); two
 prior drops -> 2 (base -> 3 capped); standing 5 -> 1 (base -> 3 capped); all-baseline 0. Near-miss: the 2026-05-02 and
 2026-06-01 drops are expired yet count as recorded for the prior-drop tier.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. dispute_window (time): anchor the violation's event_date, not_after, violation_dispute_days (Diamond 14),
 day 0, inclusive, judged at submission. Late 2026-09-16 (submitted 09-17, last day 09-30); wrong-address 09-17 (submitted
 09-18, last 10-01); alcohol 09-18 (submitted 09-19, last 10-02); dropped 09-20 (filed in-app 09-23, last 10-04). Base "any other
 dispute goes to the appeals team" and the late-delivery clearing clause are superseded clause by clause; base points stay for
 late (1) and alcohol (6).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Each submitted dispute names its violation (APw->Vw->batch bd36c439-e5bc-4308-ab72-834ed9afa9c9; APa->Va->5f4f5cfb-f865-4350-b453-444b6cfe51c1; APl->Vl->751202c8-54ee-4ebf-8e55-55b3640ba739);
 the in-app dispute concerns the most recent dropped-batch violation Vd -> d3803f78-7afa-40d8-8359-7db9a613c4c6. Older violations of the same types are expired
 and booked out and only enter the prior-count tiers.

7. SEED. customers 1, shopper_accounts 1 (balance 12 = recorded 30 - cleared 18, below Diamond hold 13), shopper_events 27 (12
 ratings, 3 exclusions, 8 violations, 4 expiry clearings), shopper_appeals 3 (all submitted), batches 12, batch_events 34. All
 three dropped batches are shopper_choice drops (the only reason the batch charter records a violation for). Historical points
 follow the charter at their booking dates (seed_consistency: Vd = 2 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 + 0 - 1 = 3; Vw = 1 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 - 1 = 2;
 Vp2 = 7). After all writes the balance is 12 - 1 - 2 - 1 - 2 = 6; no hold, warning or deactivation is ignited.

8. PERSONA. Calm, organised, formal; volunteers the dispute and the batch story; credentials only when asked; generic go-ahead for
 prerequisites; keeps no list of open items; files the dispute herself with the figures given; ends on confirmation.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, email) -> find_shopper_accounts -> find_shopper_events ->
 find_shopper_appeals -> find_batches -> find_batch_events -> decide wrong-address (1) -> decide alcohol-procedure (2) -> decide
 late-delivery (1) -> hand over the in-app dispute; the shopper files it (2).

10. VERIFICATION. check_extended / check_task_tools / replay_tasks / check_solvability / check_compute / check_grounding /
 check_cross_fire --task 1: all OK after round 2; sensitivity run printed 1, 2, 1, 2 with each skipped prerequisite giving root 1.

11. REVISIONS. Round 1: historical points aligned with the severities. Round 2 (audit F2/T1-F2): the alcohol hand-off praise credit
 is replaced by the recent-record reduction and the outage credit re-tiered (3 / 4), alcohol result 3 -> 2, root standing tiers
 6/3; wrong-address excusal low-rating tier counts ratings of 2 stars or fewer and the Triple batch carries two 2-star ratings (so
 its historical severity, now with the repeat-address surcharge, stays 2); drop severity re-derivation under the shopper_choice rule
 (Bd 26 units, Vp2 = 7); boundary checks anchored on submission.
